s: The Radcliffe Committee was appointed to
o: solve the problem of minorities in India
give effect to the Independence Bill
delimit the boundaries between India and Pakistan
enquire into the riots in East Bengal
x: The Radcliffe Line was the boundary between the Indian and Pakistani portions of the Punjab Province and Bengal Presidency of British India. It was named after Cyril Radcliffe, who served as the joint chairman of the boundary commissions for the Punjab and Bengal provinces. The demarcation line was published on 17 August 1947 upon the Partition of British India. Today, its western side is part of the India–Pakistan border, while its eastern side is the Bangladesh–India border.

o: Solve the problem of minorities in India
Give effect to the Independence Bill
Demarcate the boundaries between India and Pakistan
Enquire into the riots in East Bengal
x: Viceroy of British India, Lord Mountbatten formed two commissions namely Punjab Border Commission and Bengal Border Commission to decide the borderline between India and Pakistan on June 30, 1947 AD. Cyril Radcliffe was appointed as President of both the Commissions. Those Commissions had to demarcate borders by Muslims and Non-Muslims population. They had to consider other factors too. There were four members (judges) in each Commission of which two were from Indian National Congress and two from the Muslim League.

s: Which among the following was not one of the provisions of the Communal Award?

Separate electorates for the Europeans and the Sikhs.
The separate electorates were to lapse at the end of 10 years.

s: The purpose of Poona Pact was:
x: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates with joint electorates and reserved seats (148) for the depressed classes. Its purpose was representation of untouchables.

He wanted the Communal Award to apply only to Muslims.
He opposed all forms of political representation for the Depressed Classes.

s:
Consider the following statements:

s: What did Ambedkar demand for the Depressed Classes at the Second Round Table Conference?

s: Between whom was the Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 signed?
o: B.R. Ambedkar and Madan Mohan Malaviya

s: By what other name is the Poona Pact often known?

s: Gandhi’s fast unto death against separate electorates for the Depressed Classes took place at which jail?

s: Under the Poona Pact (1932), to how many were the reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in provincial legislatures increased from 71?

s: What was the All India Anti-Untouchability League, founded by Gandhi in 1932, later renamed?
x: The All India Anti-Untouchability League (30 September 1932) was renamed the Harijan Sevak Sangh.

s: Who is the author of “Annihilation of Caste”?

s: Which work of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, written in 1936, was a critique of Hindu orthodoxy and of Gandhi?

s: Which of the following was written by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar?

s: Which book of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, published in 1948, dealt with the origin of untouchability?

s: In which year was 'Thoughts on Linguistic States' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar published?

o: Who Were the Shudras – B.R. Ambedkar
The Problem of the Rupee – Jyotiba Phule
x: Who Were the Shudras is Ambedkar's; Gulamgiri is by Phule, while Annihilation of Caste and The Problem of the Rupee are Ambedkar's.

s: 'The Problem of the Rupee' by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was his thesis for which degree?
x: 'The Problem of the Rupee' (1923) was Ambedkar's DSc thesis at the London School of Economics.

s: Who said that, 'Nothing can emancipate the outcaste except the destruction of the caste system'?
x: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar strongly criticized the caste system and argued that social equality could not be achieved without destroying caste hierarchy. He believed that annihilation of caste was essential for the emancipation of marginalized communities.

s: Who stated that 'I measure the progress of a III. community by the degree of progress which women have achieved'?
x: The quote about measuring a community's progress by women's progress is by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

s: Who of the following said, “Mahatma Gandhi like fleeting phantom raises dust but not the level”?
x: On 14 August, 1931 A.D., Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said during a conversation with Gandhi in Mumbai “History tells that Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust but not level.” It was noted that there was a conflict between Gandhi and Ambedkar on the matter of “situations of depressed classes.” Gandhiji began fast-unto-death on 20th September, 1932 against Communal Award of Prime Minister Ramsay Macdonald. Poona Pact was signed between the followers of Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. s: Which of the following correctly contrasts Gandhi's and Ambedkar's approaches to caste?
o: Gandhi: annihilate caste through law; Ambedkar: retain varna
Gandhi: reform Hinduism, retain varna, use 'Harijan'; Ambedkar: annihilate caste through law and political power
Both: retain varna and avoid political action
Both: same approach, differing only in terminology
x: Gandhi sought to reform Hinduism, retain varna and used the term 'Harijan'; Ambedkar sought the annihilation of caste through legal and political means.

s: Which portfolio did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar hold in the Viceroy's Executive Council during 1942–46?
x: Ambedkar was Labour Member of the Viceroy's Executive Council from 1942 to 1946.

s: Over which issue did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resign as Law Minister in September 1951?
x: He resigned on 27 September 1951 over the stalled Hindu Code Bill.

s: Which term for the Depressed Classes did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar reject?
x: Ambedkar rejected Gandhi's term 'Harijan'.

s: In which year did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar make the remark 'Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust but not the level'?
x: He made the remark on 14 August 1931 in Mumbai.

s: About whom did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar make the remark 'Mahatmas, like fleeting phantoms, raise dust but not the level' in 1931?
x: Ambedkar made this remark about Gandhi in Mumbai on 14 August 1931, criticising his approach to untouchability.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said he measured the progress of a community by the degree of progress achieved by whom?
x: Ambedkar said: 'I measure the progress of a community by the degree of progress which women have achieved.'

s: Who was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946?
x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

s: Who was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly?
x: B.N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser and prepared the initial draft in October 1947.

s: Who were the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
x: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents; T.T. Krishnamachari was a Drafting Committee member.

s: B.R. Ambedkar was elected to the Constituent Assembly from:
x: He was initially elected to the Constituent Assembly from Bengal but his seat went to Pakistan following the Partition of India. He was subsequently elected from the Bombay Presidency. Since Dr Ambedkar was elected from the eastern part of undivided Bengal, not West Bengal, option (b) is the correct answer.

s: From where was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar elected to the Constituent Assembly before Partition?
x: Before Partition, Ambedkar was elected from Bengal's Jessore-Khulna area with the support of Jogendra Nath Mandal.

s: After Partition, in whose vacated seat was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar re-elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Bombay Presidency?
x: His Bengal seat went to East Pakistan, so he was re-elected from Bombay in the seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

s: Who among the following was not a member of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser who prepared the initial draft; he was not one of the Drafting Committee members. Ayyangar, Munshi and Saadullah were all members.

s: The Draft Constitution, published in February 1948, contained how many Articles?
x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948 and contained 315 Articles.

s: On which date was the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly set up?
x: It was set up on 29 August 1947 with seven members, including chairman Ambedkar; Nehru was not a member.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
o: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar — Co-author of the Munshi-Ayyangar language formula
Syed Mohammad Saadullah — Representative from Bombay
N. Madhava Rao — Original member in place of B.L. Mitter
T.T. Krishnamachari — Replaced Dr. K.M. Munshi
x: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar was associated with the Munshi-Ayyangar language formula. Saadullah was from Assam, Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter, and T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan.

s: Who was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee?
x: K.M. Munshi, who also chaired the Order of Business Committee, was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee.

s: On which date was the Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the language of the Constitution adopted?
x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on 14 September 1949. The date is also associated with the observance of Hindi Diwas on 14 September.

s: Apart from its chairman, how many other members did the Drafting Committee have?
x: The Drafting Committee had 7 members: the chairman plus 6 others.

s: For how many days did the Drafting Committee sit?
x: The Drafting Committee sat for 141 days.

s: Whom did T.T. Krishnamachari replace in the Drafting Committee?
x: T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan (died 1948); N. Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter.

s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee?
x: Nehru was not a member of the Drafting Committee; the other three were.

s: On which date was the Draft Constitution prepared by the Drafting Committee published?
x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948 with 315 Articles and 8 Schedules.

s: Which member of the Drafting Committee chaired the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: K.M. Munshi, originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee, chaired the Order of Business Committee.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described which provision as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Constitution?
x: Article 32, which guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, was described by Ambedkar as the ‘heart and soul’ of the Constitution.

s: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability?
x: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes it punishable; Articles 15-16 cover non-discrimination and Article 46 the welfare of SCs/STs.

s: What did Ambedkar hope the emergency provisions under Article 356 would remain?
o: Source of the Union’s power to secede
x: Ambedkar expressed the hope that Article 356 would remain a ‘dead letter’, indicating that it would not be used routinely.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's views in the Constituent Assembly:

2. He hoped Article 356 would remain a dead letter.

s: During the debates on its making, the Indian Constitution was criticised as a copy of which Act?
x: Critics called it a 'copy of the Government of India Act, 1935' and a 'lawyers' paradise'.

s: From whom did Ambedkar borrow the term 'constitutional morality'?
x: Ambedkar took the term from George Grote and said constitutional morality has to be cultivated.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched regarding Ambedkar's view of Indian federalism?
o: System – unitary or federal as times require
Centre – strong, to protect weaker sections
States – right to secede from the Union
x: Ambedkar held the Union indestructible, so States have no right to secede; the other pairs reflect his views.

s: In Ambedkar's view, what did India being a 'Union of States' mean?
o: States could secede by a referendum
The Union is indestructible and states have no right to secede
States are sovereign units that formed a compact
The Centre can be dissolved by the states
x: Ambedkar said the Union is indestructible and the states have no right to secede.

s: Who among the following stated in the Constituent Assembly that on January 26, 1950, India was going to enter a life of contradictions?
x: In his final speech of 25 November 1949, Ambedkar warned that on 26 January 1950 India enters a life of contradictions, with political equality but social and economic inequality.

s: On which date did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar deliver his final speech in the Constituent Assembly?
x: Ambedkar delivered his final speech in the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the three warnings given by Ambedkar in his final Constituent Assembly speech?
o: Turn political democracy into social democracy.
Abolish the parliamentary system in favour of a presidential system.
Give up the bloody methods of revolution and civil disobedience.
Do not lay liberties at the feet of a great man.
x: Ambedkar warned against violent and extra-constitutional methods, hero-worship in politics, and the failure to establish social democracy. He did not call for abolishing the parliamentary system.

s: Ambedkar's reference to India entering 'a life of contradictions' on 26 January 1950 pointed to the coexistence of which of the following?
o: Federalism with the right of secession
Political equality with social and economic inequality
x: The contradiction lay in political equality coexisting with inequality in social and economic life. Ambedkar urged that political democracy be transformed into social democracy.

s: In his final speech, what did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar call civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha?
x: He said these methods were now the 'grammar of anarchy' and should be given up.

s: According to Ambedkar, what does bhakti or hero-worship in politics lead to?
x: His second warning: bhakti or hero-worship in politics leads to dictatorship.

s: In his final speech of 25 November 1949, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said political democracy cannot last unless there lies at its base:
x: Ambedkar said political democracy cannot last unless social and economic democracy lies at its base.

s: The stalling of which Bill made Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resign as Law Minister in September 1951?
x: The omnibus Hindu Code Bill stalled in Parliament and Ambedkar resigned in September 1951.

x: The Hindu Marriage Act 1955 brought monogamy and divorce; the Hindu Succession Act 1956 made daughters Class I heirs.

x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 made daughters Class I heirs; the 2005 amendment gave them equal coparcenary rights.

s: The great law-giver of ancient times was –

s: Which title was given to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the law-giver of modern India?
x: Ambedkar is called the 'Modern Manu', the law-giver of modern India.

s: At the time of India’s Independence, Mahatma Gandhi was:
o: A member of Congress Working Committee
Not a member of the Congress
The General Secretary of the Congress
x: At the time of India’s Independence, Gandhiji was not the member of Congress. In 1934 A.D. he resigned from Congress, and after that, he never became a formal member of Congress. However, his strong guidance influenced the political scenario of India.

s: Who among the following was the first Law Minister of India?
x: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the first Law Minister of Independent India. He became the Law Minister on the recommendation of Mahatma Gandhi. He worked as the President of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.

Why Dr B.R.Ambedkar supported electorates for depressed classes?

o: Only untouchability needed to be removed while the caste system could remain.

s: On which of the following did Gandhi and Ambedkar differ fundamentally?

s: Who described caste as “not just a division of labour, but a division of labourers”?

s: On which date did Ambedkar call the Indian village 'a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism' in the Constituent Assembly?

s: What was Ambedkar's position regarding political power for the Depressed Classes?

s:

s: For which organisation was Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste (1936) prepared as an address?

s: In Annihilation of Caste, Ambedkar called which of the following the "real remedy" for caste?
x: Ambedkar held inter-caste marriage to be the real remedy; change of heart and temple entry were Gandhi's methods.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Annihilation of Caste (1936)?

It argued that the whole caste system must go
Gandhi replied to it in Harijan
It was delivered by Ambedkar at Lahore

s: According to Ambedkar's Who Were the Shudras?, who were the Shudras originally?

An occupational group created by British legislation
A group formed exclusively from foreign invaders
x: Ambedkar argued that the Shudras were originally Kshatriyas who were degraded after conflict with Brahmins, who denied them the upanayana.

s: On behalf of which organisation was States and Minorities submitted to the Constituent Assembly in 1947?

To permit every village to frame a separate economic constitution
To prevent all state ownership of industries

s: According to Ambedkar, what should be the basic unit of the Indian polity?

s: The religion which permitted widow marriage was:

s:
